name: comparator-offset-tran-extracted-feasibility
description: FEASIBILITY ONLY (issue #219): can the whole-comparator staircase transient Monte Carlo be run against the EXTRACTED binding with a valid measurement contract? Limited grid (named PVT points, small N); never a 45x200 campaign and never a reference record.
claim: NONE. A feasibility result establishes (or refuses) the measurement contract toward T1 post-layout verification; it is not signoff item 7, mints no record under any bench's records/ directory, and relaxes no ratified bound. The absolute mean trip point (deterministic layout offset + draw mean) and the random sigma are reported separately; the staircase centre is a documented stimulus choice and is never subtracted from the mean.

sig_trip_raw_mv.description: MISMATCH-ON GUARD, not a spec bound. The staircase quantises the trip point to 0.16 mV steps, so a collapsed population reads a raw sigma of 0 (one bin) or at most step/2 = 0.080 mV (two adjacent bins), and a corrected sigma of at most 0.065 mV; 0.1 mV sits above both. A deck that failed to turn local mismatch on would report ~0 here while every other number in the record still looked plausible. 0.1 mV is far below anything a real 180 nm comparator can achieve, so this floor cannot be read as a design assertion -- it only catches a collapsed (mismatch-free) population. The ratified bound (<= 15 mV 3-sigma stretch <= 8 mV, README.md, DR-0002) is deliberately NOT encoded as a check in this manifest: it is scored separately against the bound, and a sanity floor here must not be read as, or edited into, the spec verdict.
